rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Environmental claims must have clear basis (Rule 11.1)
rules.explanation: Unqualified environmental claims are likely to mislead if they omit significant information about the basis of the claim

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Absolute claims require high level of substantiation (Rule 11.3)
rules.explanation: Absolute environmental claims must be supported by comprehensive evidence covering the full product lifecycle

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Carbon neutral/net zero claims must specify if based on offsetting
rules.explanation: Must include information about whether actively reducing emissions or relying on offsetting. Consumers often wrongly assume these mean no emissions are generated

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Recyclable claims must clarify which parts and specify conditions
rules.explanation: Must make clear which parts are recyclable and whether special recycling schemes are required. Claims may mislead if recycling infrastructure is not widely available

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Must clarify what parts contain recycled content (Rule 11.1)
rules.explanation: Claims must specify whether packaging, product, or component contains recycled material. '100% recycled' claims must apply to all components including caps and labels

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Biodegradable claims must specify timeframe and conditions
rules.explanation: Must specify how long biodegradation takes and under what conditions. Consumers unaware biodegradation has unlimited timeframe and may create toxins

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Compostable claims must specify if industrial composting required
rules.explanation: Must clearly state if only suitable for industrial composting. Claims mislead if consumers assume home composting is possible when it is not

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Plastic claims must consider full lifecycle including disposal
rules.explanation: Unqualified plastic reduction claims may mislead if based only on production and not disposal. Must make clear which parts the claim applies to

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Energy claims must not imply direct supply if from National Grid
rules.explanation: Must not mislead consumers that energy comes directly from renewable sources if supplied via National Grid

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - General claims interpreted as full lifecycle unless stated otherwise (Rule 11.4)
rules.explanation: General environmental claims are likely to be interpreted as covering entire lifecycle from manufacture to disposal. Must be qualified if only applies to part of lifecycle

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Vague claims must be qualified with specific information
rules.explanation: Vague sustainability claims need qualification to explain what aspect of the product or service provides environmental benefit

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Claims about initiatives must include balancing information about overall impact
rules.explanation: Where businesses responsible for significant emissions promote specific green initiatives, must include balancing information about ongoing environmental harm to avoid misleading impression

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Future goals must be based on verifiable strategy
rules.explanation: Claims about future net zero or carbon neutrality goals must be based on verifiable strategy to deliver them, not just aspirations

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Offsetting claims must provide information about the scheme used
rules.explanation: Where carbon neutral claims based on offsetting, must provide information about the offsetting scheme and not mislead consumers into thinking emissions are being reduced

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Comparative claims must show total environmental benefit and clear basis
rules.explanation: Comparative claims like 'greener' require verifiable evidence of environmental benefit over previous product or competitors. Basis of comparison must be clear

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Must not omit material information about environmental harm (Rule 3.3)
rules.explanation: Marketing must not mislead by omitting information about adverse environmental effects or presenting such information unclearly

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - 'Widely recycled' must be substantiated by local authority evidence
rules.explanation: Claims that product is widely recycled must be supported by evidence showing it is recycled by majority of local authorities in the UK

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Must clarify if disposal differs from consumer expectations
rules.explanation: If disposal process differs from average consumer expectations, this is material information that must be clearly communicated

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Must not suggest universal acceptance if scientific opinion divided (Rule 11.5)
rules.explanation: Where significant division of scientific opinion exists, this must be made clear. Cannot suggest claims have universal acceptance

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Cannot imply improvement if product never had adverse effect (Rule 11.6)
rules.explanation: If product never had demonstrably adverse environmental effect, must not imply formulation has changed to improve it

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Cannot highlight benefit from legal obligation if competitors subject to same (Rule 11.7)
rules.explanation: Must not mislead by highlighting environmental benefit that results from legal obligation if competing products subject to same requirements

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Natural imagery may mislead if business has significant emissions without balancing info
rules.explanation: Imagery of natural world may contribute to impression of environmental credentials. May mislead for high-emission businesses without qualifying information

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Cannot present negative impact as past if still occurring
rules.explanation: Presenting environmental harm in past tense misleads if company still has significant negative impact. Suggests business has moved on from harmful activities

rules.regulation: ASA CAP - Plastic alternatives must not mislead about environmental benefit
rules.explanation: Claims about plastic alternatives must not mislead consumers about overall environmental impact considering full lifecycle
